message.content:
This is a paper cap, so I looked at the headgear headings. The candidates are 6505 (hats of textile, made up from fabric), 6506 (other headgear), and 4602 or 4823 for paper articles.

Heading 6504 covers hats and other headgear, plaited or made by assembling strips of any material. That doesn't fit a die-cut paper cap.

Heading 6506 covers other headgear, whether or not lined or trimmed. Subheading 6506.99 covers headgear of other materials, and 6506.99.60 is "Other" (of other materials).

CBP has ruled on paper party hats, which fall under 9505 as festive articles. But this cap is for promotional use. It is a baseball-style cap and the description says it is not suitable for repeated wear. It is not a festive article in the 9505 sense, though it could arguably be one for festivals. I think CBP most likely classified it in 6506.99.

The 6506.99 breakdown is:
- 6506.99.10: of fur felt
- 6506.99.20: of cotton or other vegetable fibers
- 6506.99.60: other

Paper falls under 6506.99.60. The 10-digit statistical suffix is 6506.99.6000.
